Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:57 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood, AE)
- Diego Alvarez (Redwood, SE)
- Priya Kapoor (Redwood, Solutions)
- Liam O'Connor (StratusCloud, Partnerships)
- Aisha Rahman (StratusCloud, Eng Mgr)
- Jon Park (StratusCloud, GPU Ops)
- Sven Mueller (StratusCloud, SE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Intro call between Redwood and StratusCloud to explore partnership models (resell, marketplace, technical integration). Discussed target workloads, GPU SKUs, latency and cost tradeoffs, private/VPC deployment options, KMS/tenant isolation, and next steps for benchmarks and legal intro.

Topics:
- Partner motion and commercial models
- Technical integration points (APIs, telemetry, auth)
- Performance benchmarks and compatibility (A100, H100 equivalent, NVLink)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
00:00:03 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we'll kick off with a 10 minute partner overview then transition Diego for the technical bits.
00:00:18 Liam (StratusCloud): Thanks Maya. We're excited to explore how StratusCloud can be a go-to GPU partner for Redwood, especially for your Dedicated and Private offerings.
00:00:45 Maya: Great. Quick orientation - Redwood provides hosted inference, dedicated pools, and private VPC/on-prem deployments. Our customers care about latency, cost, and observable SLAs. Not a product pitch, more to see where we overlap.
00:01:12 Sven (StratusCloud SE): Quick note, we run custom SKUs with NVLink and our "Aurora" line which maps closely to H100 performance profiles, and we do marketplace integrations.
00:01:37 Aisha (Eng): Curious about the integration surface area, is it just API keys or do you need deep networking/VPN access for Private deployments?
00:01:55 Maya: For hosted we do API keys over TLS, for Private/VPC we support customer-managed networking and optional on-prem packaging. We'll need SAML/OIDC for SSO and KMS integration for key management.
00:02:20 Diego (Redwood SE): On the runtime side, you can integrate at two levels - 1) simple API proxy where Stratus runs Redwood agents and we hit your infra, or 2) deeper marketplace/AMI approach where we distribute our runtime image and orchestration logic. The deeper model gives better telemetry and autoscaling hooks.
00:02:58 Jon (GPU Ops): When you say runtime image, do you mean you'd want control-plane connectivity back to Redwood? We're concerned about data exfil and compliance.
00:03:15 Diego: We can operate with a private control plane pattern where the control plane is customer-managed or pulled, and logs can be forwarded into your SIEM. We support envelope encryption and KMS so keys never leave customer control.
00:03:46 Maya: Also worth noting our Dedicated contracts can run in isolated VLANs and we can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted if capacity is constrained.
00:04:05 Liam: From a business perspective, we're thinking about reseller margins vs. marketplace listings. What's Redwood's typical partner split, do you prefer revenue share or referral?
00:04:22 Maya: We are flexible - many partners do marketplace listings plus revenue share for managed Dedicated, others do reseller with a markup. We'll share the partner integration checklist and options.
00:04:40 Sven: Are there any model licensing restrictions? For example, if a customer wants to bring their own model - can they run arbitrary OSS models?
00:04:58 Priya (Redwood): We support curated open models and customers can bring models as long as the model license permits the deployment. For enterprise, we often recommend verified model variants for performance and regression monitoring.
00:05:22 Aisha: On telemetry and billing, what's exposed? We need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency.
00:05:34 Diego: The Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and tracing. For private installs we can forward those metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana stack or provide a lightweight agent.
00:06:00 Jon: For benchmarking, we'd want an example load profile. Can you share what lengths/seqs you test with?
00:06:12 Diego: Typical matrix: small chat seqs (256 tokens), mid-range (512), long-form generation (2k+). We test throughput and p99 latency. We also test quantized variants for cost saving.
00:06:34 Liam: Any mandatory security certifications we should be aware of? SOC 2 is usually requested by our enterprise customers.
00:06:45 Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we can provide pen test reports and SOC documents under NDA. We also have RBAC, audit logs, and optional HSM/KMS integrations.
00:07:05 Sven: Regarding networking, does the KV cache or prefix cache leak any PII? How do you handle cache invalidation?
00:07:18 Priya: Prefix/KV caching is configurable and can be disabled. We also offer customer-scoped caches for tenant isolation and TTL-based invalidation. We can ensure no persistent PII storage in shared cache.
00:07:40 Aisha: Great. On the tech-customer side, what would you need from our infra team to run a benchmark?
00:07:52 Diego: We'll need an isolated GPU node (or access via your test env), expected network egress patterns, and sample prompts or workloads. A test SSH/console access to orchestrate the runtime or an AMI/VM image to deploy.
00:08:20 Jon: We can provision an NVLink-enabled node and sandbox networking. Estimate internal lead time of 5 business days.
00:08:38 Maya: Perfect. Quick question on quantization - do you have preferred versions? Customers often ask about 4-bit quant with minimal perf regression.
00:08:52 Diego: We support INT8 and 4-bit quantization profiles; there's a tradeoff between quality and cost. We'll run evals on your workload to recommend profiles.
00:09:10 Liam: On commercial ops, do you require minimum committed capacity for a reseller deal?
00:09:20 Maya: For Dedicated we usually discuss reserved capacity commitments; for marketplace/resell there's more flexibility. We'll share both templates.
00:09:40 (crosstalk)
00:09:58 Diego: One more technical: KV cache co-location - if you want low-latency chat, co-locating cache with the model shard reduces round trips, but that requires specific orchestration. We have orchestration knobs to pin cache and model on same node.
00:10:25 Jon: Good to know. Latency SLOs - what are realistic p99 targets for short chat on Aurora-equivalent hardware?
00:10:38 Diego: On H100-like Aurora with our runtime and batching tuned for small seqs you can expect ~60-120ms p99 for single-turn chat at modest concurrency; throughput depends on batching and concurrency patterns. We'll provide benchmark numbers.
00:10:58 Aisha: That latency variance is big; customers will want tighter SLOs. Can Redwood provide SLA-backed latency or is it uptime-only?
00:11:10 Maya: We offer SLA-backed uptime; latency SLAs are available for Dedicated in contract via configuration and reserved throughput. We can include p99 latency targets in Dedicated contracts.
00:11:30 Liam: From a partner integration perspective, we're also thinking about joint go-to-market - co-marketing, references, maybe early access to pilot customers.
00:11:45 Maya: Absolutely. We often do joint case studies and go-to-market motions. We'll coordinate with your marketplace and partner teams.
00:11:57 Sven: Any red flags from your side about StratusCloud? We want to be transparent.
00:12:05 Maya: Nothing major. We'll want to validate your security posture and the audit evidence. Also clarity on support SLAs and escalation paths for Dedicated customers.
00:12:20 Jon: Support - we can offer L2 escalation and a dedicated channel for Redwood partners.
00:12:30 (short silence)
00:12:45 Diego: Quick dive - how are you provisioning GPUs today? Are you mostly selling managed instances or bare-metal racks?
00:12:58 Liam: We offer both. Our Aurora rack is bare-metal with NVLink; we also expose managed instances with tenant isolation. We do a marketplace image for certain ISVs.
00:13:15 Priya: For the marketplace flow, would StratusCloud host a Redwood runtime image, or would we publish a connector?
00:13:27 Sven: We prefer an image/AMI to lower friction for customers, but we can also host connectors. Image gives faster onboarding.
00:13:40 Priya: Good. For private installs, auth options - do you need SAML inbound or can you integrate via OAuth/OIDC?
00:13:51 Aisha: We can do both. We have an enterprise SSO stack and can accept SAML assertions or OIDC flows.
00:14:05 Diego: Then the auth flow is straightforward. For encryption at rest we recommend integrating an HSM/KMS - we'll provide integration docs for AWS KMS / customer HSMs.
00:14:20 Liam: On billing and metering - do you expose per-token usage for partners to pass through to end customers?
00:14:32 Maya: Yes, token-level metering is available and we can export usage reports for billing reconciliation. For marketplace flows, we can emit a usage feed or integrate with your billing APIs.
00:15:00 (pause)
00:15:15 Priya: If we run a benchmark, we should pick 3 workloads - chat, instruction-following, embeddings - to measure both latency and throughput. Diego can own the matrix.
00:15:30 Diego: Agreed. Also include model variants and quantized runs. We'll also instrument p99 and p50, memory utilization, and GPU efficiency.
00:15:50 Jon: We'll prepare a test node and give network details. Expect 5 business days to provision.
00:16:05 Liam: On legal, what's the path to a reseller agreement? We have standard partner T&Cs but will need Redwood's legal to review.
00:16:18 Maya: We'll share a reseller template. Typically we do an MoU, then test pilot, then an MSA + SOW for Dedicated. I'll get Legal looped in.
00:16:35 Sven: Quick technical Q - do you require RDMA or can you work over standard TCP?
00:16:45 Diego: The runtime can work over TCP, but RDMA/NVLink gives better bandwidth for sharded model workloads. For single-GPU workloads, TCP is fine.
00:17:03 Aisha: For monitoring, what metrics do you need exposed from our side?
00:17:12 Priya: Node health, GPU utilization, temperature, memory, network egress, and optionally per-request tracing. Prometheus exporters are ideal.
00:17:28 Jon: We'll expose those.
00:17:40 (background noise)
00:18:00 Maya: We're at ~18 minutes, let's do a 10 minute technical deep dive on rerouting and fallbacks. Diego?
00:18:12 Diego: Sure. Our smart routing can route by policy - latency, cost, region, or customer tier. If a Dedicated pool is saturated, requests can failover to a cheaper hosted variant or a smaller model. That implies model compatibility mapping and quality fallbacks.
00:18:42 Liam: Do you do automatic fallback to a quantized variant? That might change output quality.
00:18:53 Diego: We can fallback to a compatible quantized or smaller variant, but we flag quality regression and can attach evals to monitor. We also support per-route fallback policies so customers choose tradeoffs.
00:19:20 Aisha: On data residency - if a customer wants EU-only data residency and we run in your hosted plane, do you offer region pinning?
00:19:32 Maya: Yes, region pinning is available; for stricter residency we recommend Private deployment.
00:19:45 Jon: On the topic of benchmarks, assume we run a 30-minute steady-state test; what telemetry do you collect?
00:19:56 Diego: We collect request/response latencies, batch sizes, GPU memory and SM utilization, and KV cache hit rates. We'll share a CSV and dashboard.
00:20:12 (short gap)
00:21:05 Liam: Switching to go-to-market, we're curious about co-sell motions and referral models. Do you provide partner enablement material?
00:21:18 Maya: Yes, we have partner enablement kits, technical playbooks, and sales training - we'll put you through a partner onboarding.
00:21:32 Sven: Any restrictions on being a reseller if we also resell other LLM vendors?
00:21:40 Maya: No exclusivity required. We prefer strategic alignment but partners often resell multiple infra providers.
00:21:58 (noise)
00:22:20 Diego: Quick note about private deployments - we can run in customer VPC and support private control plane patterns. That requires some onboarding effort (networking, firewall rules, certs) but it's a standard process.
00:22:40 Jon: We'll want docs for the firewall and Egress rules.
00:22:48 Priya: We'll send a checklist with ports, certs, and AMI details.
00:22:55 Maya: Ok we're at ~25 minutes, big picture recap then next steps.
00:23:05 Maya: Recap - both sides interested in marketplace + reseller and Dedicated flows. Technical BAU: run benchmarks, validate network and security posture, and exchange legal contacts. Owners as discussed.
00:23:22 Liam: Sounds good. Anything else?
00:23:30 Aisha: One more - for model governance, do you support eval hooks or custom eval sets?
00:23:40 Diego: Yes, we wire eval pipelines and regression alerts; customers can upload prompt sets and we run nightly or on-deploy evals.
00:23:55 Sven: Nice.
00:24:05 Maya: Alright, let's capture next steps. (brief pause)
00:24:18 Maya: Action items captured - I'll send the deck + partner template; Diego will prep benchmark matrix; Priya will share integration checklist. Liam will loop marketplace and legal.
00:24:40 Liam: We'll get the test node ready and connect your SEs.
00:24:55 Maya: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the technical deep-dive and benchmark window.
00:25:05 End of formal discussion. Remaining minutes used for quick side Q&A and informal notes.
00:31:10 (informal) Jon: One thought - if we co-bundle a managed offering, what would support look like?
00:31:25 Maya: We offer tiered support; partners get partner SLA and joint escalation.
00:34:50 (crosstalk)
00:40:15 Aisha: On the billing feed format, can you accept flat CSV or do you have an API?
00:40:30 Priya: We have both - flat CSV export and a usage API for automated pulls.
00:45:02 (end mumbled logistics)
00:55:10 Maya: Final wrap - thanks everyone. We'll send the follow ups.
00:56:05 Liam: Thanks, talk soon.
00:56:50 Recording stopped.

Call ended with clear next steps and owners.
